messages:
alex_chen: Hey team — I sketched an RFC for customer-managed networking for Private deployments. Link: https://docs.internal/redwood/rfcs/customer-managed-networking (WIP). TL;DR: support per-tenant static egress, BGP peering, and optional IPSec tunnels. Asking: scope for MVP, concrete launch criteria, and acceptance tests.

maria_gupta: skimmed it — nice. My immediate concern: MVP needs a safe fallback if BGP sessions flap. We can’t have traffic blackholed.

sam_wu: +1. Also need clear contract for who configures route filters on the customer side vs us. For some customers we only provide ASN and primary prefix.

alex_chen: Agreed. Proposal in the doc: MVP = managed egress NAT + static outbound IP per-tenant + optional bgp session that is passive on our side. v1 = active peering + route exchange and prefix validation.

eddy_k: Passive BGP on our side reduces blast radius. But how do we handle overlapping prefixes? Acceptance criteria should include automatic detection and a fail-to-NAT mode.

sara_devex: From DX perspective, we need a clear runbook and terraform snippets customers can paste. Can we provide a sample minimal config block?

alex_chen: Yup. Example in RFC (copy below):
```
# customer sample: cisco IOS minimal BGP
router bgp 65001
  neighbor 203.0.113.10 remote-as 65010
  neighbor 203.0.113.10 ebgp-multihop 2
  network 198.51.100.0 mask 255.255.255.0
!
# our side will accept only exact prefixes from ASN and reject supernets
```

maria_gupta: Nice. For testing, we should include: 1) session up/down simulation, 2) prefix withdrawal handling, 3) traffic path validation, 4) ACL/port reachability tests. Each must have pass/fail criteria.

sam_wu: Edge case: customer wants to do policy NAT + hairpinning inside their network causing asymmetric flows. We should document we don't support hairpin NAT for MVP. Put that in acceptance criteria.

eddy_k: Also add rate limits on route updates; stop accepting more than X updates per minute from a peer. Otherwise noisy routers can DDoS our control plane.

alex_chen: Good call. Proposed acceptance criteria (short):
- BGP session establishes and stays up for 10 minutes under normal conditions.
- On prefix conflict, traffic falls back to per-tenant NAT IP without interruption.
- Prefix validation: only allowed prefixes from customer ASN are installed.
- Automated test harness can inject route withdraws and assert traffic continuity.
- Documentation and runbook published in Console and github repo.

sara_devex: Launch criteria checklist request: who signs off? I propose: eng-platform for architecture, eng-sre for runbooks & testing, product for customer comms, compliance for any egress controls.

maria_gupta: +1. Also add one reference customer willing to pilot (production-like load) before GA. We should have an SLA nuance in pilot contracts.

sam_wu: Operational notes: we need telemetry hooks — per-peer bgp state, prefix count, last-update-rate, and a circuit-level peer-muted flag for incidents. ADT for alerts: >80% prefix churn in 5m -> paging.

eddy_k: What about NAT? customers frequently need stable egress IPs for allowlists. We should support both static DNAT and a pool with sticky source IP by session id. MVP choose sticky by flow hash.

alex_chen: Plan: MVP supports single static egress IP per-tenant (configurable), and a fallback shared pool if the dedicated IP cannot be advertised. We will clearly document failover semantics.

sara_devex: Docs: include sample terraform snippet and Console UI mockups. Also add a short FAQ for common firewall rules (ports 443 outbound, healthcheck IPs).

maria_gupta: Security edge case: customer asks for BGP MD5 authentication. We should support MD5 on sessions. Acceptance: session with MD5 established in test harness.

sam_wu: Another edge case: customer sends more specific routes that overlap our infra CIDRs. We must filter any prefixes that cover our infra. Add explicit deny list and validation step in onboarding.

eddy_k: Rollout approach: 1) internal dogfood on staging, 2) invite-only pilot with 2 customers (one cloud-native, one on-prem firewall-heavy), 3) GA. Each step gated by acceptance tests and SRE runbook signoff.

alex_chen: Resource ask: need 2 engineers (1 infra, 1 runtime) + 1 SRE half-time for 6 sprints. Product: please confirm prioritization vs other Private tasks.

sara_devex: Product (cc @eddy_k) — can you confirm prioritization?

eddy_k: We're slotting this Q2 endpoint-infra work as medium priority. If Finserve or BetaBank commit pilot revenue, we bump to high. For now plan medium.

maria_gupta: One more test: failover from BGP to NAT must be under 500ms for traffic continuity for short RPC-style calls. Can we meet that?

sam_wu: 500ms might be tight. We can aim for 1s for RPCs and document the SLO. Add perf test to validate.

alex_chen: Noted — update RFC: change failover SLO to 1s and include a perf test that runs 10k small requests during withdrawal.

sara_devex: I'll draft the runbook and example terraform tomorrow, post link here for review.

infra-bot: New RFC uploaded: customer-managed-networking-v0.3 (doc id: rfc-2026-042). Reviewers assigned: eng-platform, eng-sre, product.

alex_chen: Thanks all — I'll incorporate feedback and update the acceptance criteria table. Please add any high-risk items you think should be escalated.
